artifact.grammar: The phrase "its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent" is a participial clause attached to the main clause. It has no finite verb like "had" with a subject; instead it uses "having + past participle" to show an action completed before the main situation. It gives the background or reason for the house's condition. In everyday English, you can turn it into a separate clause: "its residents had long ago moved to mainland Europe."
